title: CI: migrate to BuildKit multi-stage builders, remote layer cache, and toolchain refresh
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: CI runs are slow and noisy due to large, monolithic Docker base images, duplicated dependency installs across jobs, and brittle local caching. This increases feedback time for engineers and drives up runner minutes/compute spend.

Goal: Reduce average CI runtime for core service builds by >=40%, cut Docker image layer churn, and standardize build toolchains across languages (Python, TypeScript, Rust). We will: adopt BuildKit + docker/buildx for reproducible multi-stage builds; enable a remote layer cache (S3-backed registry + Docker registry cache or buildkit cache exporter); introduce language-specific slim builder images to avoid installing all toolchains on every job; and update linting/toolchain (ruff >=0.11, black >=24, typescript toolchain to node16->node20 via Volta, cargo toolchains pinned).

Outcomes: faster PR feedback, lower CI cost, smaller pushed artifacts, clearer owner for base image updates, and deterministic cache priming strategy for infra and platform teams.
comments: 2025-06-03 — Aisha Kaur: Ticket created after spike measuring median build time for infra/* services (current median: 14m). Attached perf spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/ci-build-times. Initial scope limited to 'infra' and 'runtime' services to keep rollout safe.

2025-06-05 — Miguel Torres: Spike summary: BuildKit with --cache-to type=registry reduced cold build time from 14m -> 8m when cache primed. Warm builds dropped to 2m. We saw ~28% reduction in network egress when using layered caching. PR sketch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4121.

2025-06-07 — Benji Park (Platform): Design note — prefer S3-backed buildkit cache-exporter to avoid introducing a new stateful Redis service. Need to ensure cache auth uses short-lived creds via CI OIDC. See Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/BuildKit+Cache+Design.

2025-06-09 — Security review (Emily Zhang): Reviewed OIDC usage and S3 policy. Recommendation: enforce object-level encryption (SSE-KMS) and least-privilege role for runners. Marking security_review_required=false on ticket after actions assigned to infra on rollout checklist.

2025-06-11 — Miguel Torres: Implemented builder image variants: builder-python-slim, builder-node-slim, builder-rust-slim. Pushed images to staging-registry: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/builder-*. Dockerfiles in infra/ci/builders/. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4156. Observations: python stage needs cache priming for pip wheels; using pip cache mounted into buildkit cache improved install times by 60%.

2025-06-14 — QA: Nightly runs stable. Two flaky jobs identified: lint:typescript (timeout) and publish:artifact (permissions). Created ENG-33123 and ENG-33124 for follow-ups. Planning gradual rollout and feature-flagging cache-export in Actions workflows.

2025-06-17 — Miguel Torres: Rollout step 1 completed: infra and runtime jobs enabled BuildKit cache-export to staging registry and switched to buildx. Measured median build time improvement for those jobs: 46% reduction. Next: expand to top-20 CI consumers and add cost dashboard entry (Grafana).
